sentences.text:
This petition is filed under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure (for short 'Cr.P.C.') to quash the proceedings in C.C. No.352 of 2020 on the file of learned Judicial First Class Magistrate,
Kamareddy District against the petitioners-accused Nos.1, 2, 4 and 5.
2.

entities.text:
Judicial First Class Magistrate,
Kamareddy District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Heard Sri Vijay B Paropkari, learned counsel for the petitioners, Ms. Dhanalakshmi, learned counsel representing learned counsel for the unofficial respondent and Mr.E.Ganesh, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent No.1-State.
3.

The petitioners are accused Nos. 1, 2, 4 and 5 in C.C No.352 of 2020 registered for the offences under Sections 420, 290 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC').
4.

The brief facts of the case are that on 15.11.2019 at about 13.15 hours the de-facto complainant (LW1) by name Md. Zakir Hussain, S/o.Rouful Hussain, R/o.
EVV,J Kamareddy lodged a Telugu scribed complaint, wherein it is stated that one Ghousia Begum and Rehana Begum are the absolute owners of two plots in Sy.Nos.68/1 and 68/2 admeasuring 223.5 square feet each located at Sircilla Road, Kamareddy.

It is further alleged that one Md. Irfan,
S/o. Osma, who is the son of Gousia offered to sell both the plots to him and Md. Mosin on 16.07.2019, as such, the said offer was accepted @ Rs.29,000/- per square feet.

Accordingly they paid Rs.5,00,000/- for each of the plots aggregating to Rs.10,00,000/- as advance and thereafter another some of Rs.40,00,000/- has been paid for both the plots and thus, in total an amount of Rs.50,00,000/- has been paid and to that extent an agreement of sale has been executed and a separate receipt has also been given and both the parties have agreed to proceed with the registration in the month of December, 2019 upon receipt of the balance consideration.

Thereafter,
documents have been prepared for registration by paying challan and submitted before the office of registration, Kamareddy on 16.09.2019.

Despite the said fact, the accused have not come forward to convey the sale deed and not responded to EVV,J the telephonic calls made by the de-facto complainant and it was stated by the accused that they wanted to sell the plots and for more price and thereby denied for registration of the plots nor returning the money advanced to them.

On the persistent requests, the accused have abused the de-facto complainant and threatened them with dire consequences and also on 07.11.2019 the accused persons have come to their houses and threatened and accordingly prayed for necessary action.

5. Based upon the above said complaint, the Inspector of Police, Kamareddy Police Station (LW7)
registered a case in Crime No.491/2019 for the offence under Sections 420, 290 and 506 of IPC and Mohammad Irfan And 3 Others vs The State Of Telangana And Another on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5754096/
1 investigation has been conducted.

sentences.text: During the course of investigation, as many as seven witnesses have been examined and their statements were recorded in part - II Case diary and charge sheet has been laid.
The learned Trial Court took cognizance of the said case vide C.C.No.352 of 2020.
Aggrieved by the said cognizance taken by the learned trial Court, this Criminal Petition has been filed.
EVV,J 6.

The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners while relying on the decision of the Honourable Apex Court in Radheyshyam and others v. State of Rajasthan and another 1 would submit that the substance of the case on hand are similar to the facts in the order passed by the Honourable Supreme Court and since the case on hand does not constitute an offence committed by the petitioners under Section 420 of IPC where Section 415 of IPC is not made out and except the civil proceedings nothing would subsist under criminal law.

entities.text: Radheyshyam and others v. State of Rajasthan and another 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He would further submit that the civil proceedings have been before the Principal District Judge, Kamareddy, wherein the plaintiff/defacto complainant has filed suit for specific performance and the same is pending for consideration and the entire dispute is pertaining to civil proceedings and the ingredients of criminal cases do not attract against the petitioners.

Under these circumstances, the learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that subjecting the petitioners to face the trial would amount to abuse of process of law and thus prayed to allow the petition.
2024
LiveLaw (595) EVV,J 7.

Opposing the same, Ms. Dhanalaxmi, learned counsel for the unofficial respondent while filing counter would submit that the respondent/police conducted investigation in accordance with law and the statements necessary witnesses were recorded and those witnesses have to be examined by the learned trial Court along and only after conducting thorough trial, truth will be elicited and hence seeks to dismiss the criminal petition.
8.

On the other hand, the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor would submit that unless trial is completed, truth cannot be elicited and interference of this Court in the trial Court is not warranted and hence seeks to dismiss the petition.

9. Perused the material available on record.
10.

Having heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned counsel for the unofficial respondent and learned Assistant Public Prosecutor and upon perusal of the contents of charge sheet and the orders passed by the Honourable Supreme Court in Radheyshyam's case EVV,J (supra), this Court is of the opinion that in the above said decision the Honourable Supreme Court quashed the proceedings at the stage of FIR and whereas in the case on hand the investigating agency has completed investigation and the case has been taken cognizance by the trial Court.
11. In any case, the learned trial Court is seized of the matter and the subject matter is pending since 2020 onwards and by now five years have elapsed.

Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that the Mohammad Irfan And 3 Others vs The State Of Telangana And Another on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5754096/
2 learned trial Court shall proceed with the trial in accordance with law.

sentences.text:
In the meanwhile, as sought by the learned counsel for the petitioners, the petitioners are granted liberty to file appropriate petitions including discharge petition before the learned trial Court and upon filing such petition,
the trial Court shall dispose of the said petition on merits and pass appropriate orders as expeditiously as possible preferably within three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

12. Further, as sought by the learned counsel for the petitioners, the appearance of the petitioners-accused EVV,J Nos.1, 2, 4 and 5 is dispensed with in C.C No.352 of 2020 on the file of learned Judicial First Class Magistrate, Kamareddy District, when represented by his counsel on record.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate, Kamareddy District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appearance of the petitioners-accused Nos.1, 2, 4 and 5 is dispensed with subject to filing an affidavit by the petitioners stating that in their absence, the proceedings conducted by their counsel will not be disputed by them in any manner and shall not dispute their identity also.
However, the petitioners-accused Nos.1, 2, 4 and 5 shall appear before the learned Judicial First Class Magistrate, Kamareddy District as and when their presence is required.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate, Kamareddy District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In the event of failure of the petitioners to appear when the trial Court directs, this order dispensing with their appearance shall stand cancelled automatically.
13. With the above observation, this petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.
